examples.question_text: In triangle $PQR$, let $QR=p$, $PR=q$ and $PQ=r$. Draw an altitude from $Q$ to the line $PR$. Prove that the area $K=\frac12pq\sin R$, and explain why the result also holds when $R$ is obtuse.

In acute triangle $PQR$, let the opposite sides be $p$, $q$ and $r$. Draw $RD$ perpendicular to $PQ$. Use the altitude to prove the full sine rule and its reciprocal form. Then show how it reduces to a right-triangle sine ratio when $P=90^\circ$.

In acute triangle $PQR$, let $QR=p$, $PR=q$ and $PQ=r$. Draw $RD$ perpendicular to $PQ$, with $D$ between $P$ and $Q$. Use right-angled trigonometry and Pythagoras to prove $p^2=q^2+r^2-2qr\cos P$. Hence express $\cos P$ in terms of the sides.
Triangle $PQR$ has obtuse angle $P$, with $QR=p$ and $PR=q$. Draw $RD$ perpendicular to $QP$ extended beyond $P$. Prove $\frac{p}{\sin P}=\frac{q}{\sin Q}$ using the supplementary angle identity.

Triangle $PQR$ has obtuse angle $P$, with opposite sides $p$, $q$ and $r$. Draw $RD$ perpendicular to $QP$ extended beyond $P$, and let $PD=d$. Prove the cosine rule and explain why the side opposite $P$ satisfies $p^2>q^2+r^2$.
For triangle $PQR$ with opposite sides $p$, $q$ and $r$, write its area using each included angle in turn. Use the three expressions to deduce the reciprocal sine rule.
examples.solution_text:
Each base and its corresponding altitude give the same area $K$:
$K=\frac12qr\sin P=\frac12pr\sin Q=\frac12pq\sin R$.
Multiplying by $2$ and dividing each expression by the positive product $pqr$ gives
$\begin{aligned}\frac{qr\sin P}{pqr}&=\frac{pr\sin Q}{pqr}=\frac{pq\sin R}{pqr}\\\frac{\sin P}{p}&=\frac{\sin Q}{q}=\frac{\sin R}{r}.\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Place $R$ at the origin and $Q$ on the positive horizontal axis, with $RQ=p$ and $RP=q$. Let $PQ=r$. Express the coordinates of $P$ using angle $R$, then derive the cosine rule using the distance formula.
Triangle $PQR$ has opposite sides $p$, $q$ and $r$. Starting with $K=\frac12pq\sin R$, use the sine rule to express the area using only side $p$ and angles $P$, $Q$ and $R$.
examples.solution_text:
The sine rule gives
$\begin{aligned}\frac{p}{\sin P}&=\frac{q}{\sin Q}\\q&=\frac{p\sin Q}{\sin P}.\end{aligned}$
Substitute this expression for $q$ into the area rule:
$\begin{aligned}K&=\frac12pq\sin R\\&=\frac12p\left(\frac{p\sin Q}{\sin P}\right)\sin R\\&=\frac{p^2\sin Q\sin R}{2\sin P}.\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: With QR=p and PR=q, the perpendicular height is h=p sin R, giving K=qh/2=pq sin R/2. For obtuse R, h=p sin(180°−R)=p sin R. The diagram consistently illustrates the acute construction.

RD=q sin P=p sin Q gives p/sin P=q/sin Q. The altitude from P gives r sin Q=q sin R, completing the full rule. Division by pq gives its reciprocal form. With P=90°, p=q/sin Q, hence sin Q=q/p. Diagram sides and altitude agree.
PD=x=q cos P and RD=h=q sin P. Thus p²=h²+(r−x)²=q²(sin²P+cos²P)+r²−2qr cos P=q²+r²−2qr cos P. Rearrangement gives cos P=(q²+r²−p²)/(2qr). Diagram segments and right-angle marker are consistent.
The exterior angle RPD is 180°−P, so h=q sin(180°−P)=q sin P. Also h=p sin Q. Equating and dividing by sin P sin Q yields p/sin P=q/sin Q. The diagram places D beyond P and correctly shows obtuse P.

PD=d=q cos(180°−P)=−q cos P and h²+d²=q². Therefore p²=h²+(r+d)²=q²+r²+2rd=q²+r²−2qr cos P. Since cos P<0, p²>q²+r². Both acute and obtuse base expressions equal r−q cos P. Diagram geometry and labels agree.
The area expressions are 2K=qr sin P=pr sin Q=pq sin R. Dividing by positive pqr gives sin P/p=sin Q/q=sin R/r. No diagram is needed for this algebraic deduction.

P=(q cos R,q sin R) and Q=(p,0). Hence r²=(p−q cos R)²+q² sin²R=p²−2pq cos R+q²(cos²R+sin²R)=p²+q²−2pq cos R. Negative horizontal coordinates for obtuse R preserve the derivation. The diagram consistently illustrates the acute coordinate case.
The sine rule gives q=p sin Q/sin P. Substitution into K=pq sin R/2 gives K=p² sin Q sin R/(2 sin P). This is the retained assessed substitution method and requires no diagram.
